title: Balanced Tripartition
statementMd:
You are given a positive integer n>1𝑛>1. Your task is to partition the set {1,2,...,3n}{1,2,...,3𝑛} into three sets A𝐴, B𝐵, and C𝐶, each containing n𝑛 elements. The sets A𝐴, B𝐵, and C𝐶 should have the same sum. It can be shown that under the given constraints, a valid partition always exists.

## Input

Each test contains multiple test cases. The first line contains the number of test cases t𝑡 (1≤t≤501≤𝑡≤50). The description of the test cases follows.

Each test case consists of a single line containing an integer n𝑛 (2≤n≤10002≤𝑛≤1000) — the required size of each set.

It is guaranteed that the sum of n𝑛 over all test cases does not exceed 10001000.

## Output

For each test case, output a single line consisting of 3n3𝑛 characters. Each character should be either `A`, `B`, or `C` (upper or lower case). The character at position i𝑖 indicates which set the number i𝑖 belongs to (A𝐴, B𝐵, or C𝐶).

If there are multiple solutions, you may print any.

## Note

In the first test case, n=4𝑛=4, so we are splitting up the numbers from 11 to 3⋅4=123⋅4=12. One solution is to partition these numbers into A={1,7,8,10}𝐴={1,7,8,10}, B={2,3,9,12}𝐵={2,3,9,12}, and C={4,5,6,11}𝐶={4,5,6,11}. Each of these sets contains 44 numbers and sums to 2626. Since 11 is in A𝐴, the first character of our output is `A`. Since 22 is in B𝐵, the second character of our output is `B`. Carrying on this process, we obtain the output `ABBCCCAABACB`.
